title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Lightning humanoid sprint

### The Breakthrough
Lightning, a humanoid built by Honor, sprinted 100 m in 9.32 s, reaching a peak speed of 14.5 m/s thanks to 95 cm‑long legs with a 10 cm extension, high‑torque actuators and balance control. This hardware demonstrates versatile locomotion across sprint, half‑marathon, and high‑jump tasks, a first at this scale.

### The Caveats
The record‑breaking sprint is a single, controlled event compared only to human world records, lacking a meaningful robotic baseline.

## Video2DoorTraversal

### The Breakthrough
A single RGB video is turned into a DoorTwin simulation model, enabling a policy that opens and traverses doors with 96.57 % success on five real doors and 80.95 % zero‑shot on unseen doors, completing the task in about 13 s.

### The Caveats
Success rates are reported without comparison to existing door‑opening baselines.

## MILD deformable terrain

### The Breakthrough
MILD’s discrete‑element contact solver supplies richer foot‑ground data to a latent‑modulated DRL controller, letting a biped identify and walk on yielding surfaces with better real‑world adaptation than prior simulators.

### The Caveats
The paper does not specify which baselines were used, so improvements cannot be independently verified.

## GEN-1.5 foundation model

### The Breakthrough
GEN‑1.5 ingests up to 30 s of video, language, and proprioception, outputting 100 Hz action trajectories; it acquires a new dexterous skill from a single 3‑12 s demonstration (59 % one‑shot success, 83 % after few‑shot fine‑tuning).

### The Caveats
One‑shot success rates lack comparison to prior methods, leaving the magnitude of improvement unverified.

## DECOWAM whole‑body model

### The Breakthrough
DECOWAM extends FastWAM with conditional adapters and adversarially separated base/arm latents, cutting action MSE by 21.7 % and showing superior coordination in 79 closed‑loop trials on a legged platform.

### The Caveats
Evaluation is limited to the ARMDOG dataset and a single robot, with no varied terrain or morphology tests.

## PVRA assembly voting

### The Breakthrough
PVRA uses pointwise key‑point voting on RGB‑D input to infer assembly dependencies and relative poses, outperforming generic object‑centric baselines on a pose‑estimation dataset.

### The Caveats
The approach is tested only in simulation on a dataset, without real‑robot experiments.

## MowgliNext mower stack

### The Breakthrough
The ROS2 stack fuses RTK‑GPS, IMU, wheel odometry and optional LiDAR via GTSAM iSAM2, delivering claimed sub‑centimeter positioning, strip‑by‑strip coverage planning, auto‑docking and a web‑based GUI for autonomous mowing.

### The Caveats
Claims of sub‑centimeter accuracy and a complete pipeline lack quantitative results or benchmarks.

## Qwen reverse engineering

### The Breakthrough
Running locally on a workstation, Qwen‑3.8 27B uses speculative decoding to disassemble an ARM64 binary, recover its RSA verification key and generate a working license‑bypass script in ~30 minutes, all offline.

### The Caveats
The test is informal and limited to a single binary, with no comparison to existing tools.

## Spec‑d‑model 3D ramp

### The Breakthrough
The author splits a complex geometry into ordered specifications, prompting an LLM to generate Blender‑mcp Python code that builds a functional wedge ramp, released as an open‑source spec‑d‑model repo.

### The Caveats
Effectiveness is shown only on a single anecdotal ramp demo, without systematic benchmarking.

## Swarm foraging Q‑learning

### The Breakthrough
The repo implements fully distributed Q‑learning where each agent maintains its own NumPy Q‑table, learning to forage in a configurable grid‑world with renewable resources and dynamic obstacles, all driven by a YAML config.

### The Caveats
No quantitative evaluation or comparison to existing multi‑agent RL methods is provided.

### What to watch
Several papers (MILD, DECOWAM, Video2DoorTraversal, GEN‑1.5, PVRA) illustrate a convergence on sim‑to‑real pipelines that couple richer physics or perception models with learned policies for whole‑body coordination. Progress in terrain‑aware locomotion, door handling, and assembly reasoning suggests upcoming benchmarks that blend manipulation and locomotion.

### Priority
Lightning’s record‑breaking sprint offers the most tangible evidence of rapid hardware advances in humanoid locomotion, setting a clear benchmark for speed that other robotics efforts can reference.

### One action
Monitor the World Humanoid Robot Games releases for Lightning’s motion data and any follow‑up hardware details.
